headline: Beauty traditions precede commercial creams
body: Preferences for lighter skin appear in multiple historical contexts; the exhibition rejects a single-origin account.
caveat: Do not assign a universal start date to colourism.

headline: Hazeline line sold as skin care
body: British manufacturer Burroughs Wellcome marketed Hazeline products first around hygiene and skin care, ahead of later beauty and whitening language.
caveat: Heritage/medical claims not identical to subsequent Indian ads.

headline: Snow enters the copy
body: A British Hazeline Snow leaflet advertised the effect of making skin soft and white.
caveat: British item, not confirmed as India-specific.

headline: Burroughs Wellcome opens Bombay branch
body: Global pharmaceutical advertising and local Indian marketing become connected through a formal branch.
caveat: Branch year documented in archival academic article.

headline: Afghan Snow launches
body: E. S. Patanwala’s brand made a locally produced Indian beauty cream part of the category; snow imagery helped circulate complexion ideals.
caveat: 1919 date is reported history; keep source attribution.

headline: Hazeline Snow in Indian press
body: The Hindu carried Hazeline Snow product advertising in October 1930.
caveat: Indian original reproduced in Cambridge article; reproduction clearance pending.

headline: Shiseido Whitening Cream
body: Shiseido lists a Whitening Cream within its modern facial-care programme.
caveat: Comparative case, not evidence of identical cultural dynamics.

headline: The modern woman appears in Hazeline advertising
body: Indian print advertisements increasingly paired creams with women and modern beauty imagery.
caveat: Historical interpretation drawn from academic archive research.

headline: Independence; whitening rhetoric survives
body: After independence, corporate discussions still promoted local appeal of Hazeline’s skin-whitening effect.
caveat: 1950 company correspondence documented in archival research.

headline: Fair & Lovely reaches the market
body: Reporting dates pilot/test marketing to March 1975; HUL’s own anniversary chronology dates its launch to 1978.
caveat: Show both dates with source labels, not one artificially certain date.

headline: From personal care to social aspiration
body: Beauty marketing links complexion with marriage, romance, self-confidence and work; competition expands.
caveat: Advertising messages are not proof of real economic returns.

headline: GlutaMAX “From ebony to Ivory”
body: A documented ad uses a stark before/after complexion transformation.

headline: Fairness-advertising guidelines
body: ASCI warns against associating dark skin with unhappiness, inferior status, marriage disadvantage or reduced employment prospects.
caveat: A self-regulatory guideline, not proof violations ended.

headline: “White makes you win”
body: Seoul Secret’s Snowz supplement campaign causes criticism and is removed.
caveat: Avoid presenting one campaign as representative of all Thailand.

headline: Fair & Lovely becomes Glow & Lovely
body: HUL describes a 2019 messaging shift to glow and radiance, followed by 2020 renaming.
caveat: Company states formulation evolved and product is not bleaching cream.

headline: Mercury rule strengthens
body: Minamata Convention parties decide to remove a 1ppm threshold from the cosmetics phase-out provision.

headline: Illegal-product warnings continue
body: Trading Standards warns about hazardous products; later alerts show illegal skin-lightening cosmetics in diverse retail settings and online.
caveat: Geographic UK case study, not Asia prevalence.

headline: Two different market measures
body: Global skin-lightening forecast: US$13.2bn; entire India skincare estimate: US$2.98bn. These are not comparable categories.
caveat: Both figures from commercial firms; 2026 global forecast not observed revenue.
